introduction: The Techniques in Virology virtual lab is an interactive and practical learning tool that introduces and explores fundamental and advanced techniques used within virology. Due to strict biosafety regulations, high containment facility requirements (BSL-2/BSL-3), and costly consumables, practical training in virology is often limited within traditional teaching environments. This virtual lab provides students with an engaging, intuitive, and safe platform to explore these essential laboratory workflows. Through 10 comprehensive experimental modules, students learn how to isolate viruses from biological samples, extract and purify viral nucleic acids (RNA/DNA), quantify viral loads using real-time PCR (qPCR), and determine infectious viral titre via plaque assays and the median tissue culture infectious dose (TCID50) method. The lab also introduces critical serological and immunological diagnostics including hemagglutination (HA), hemagglutination inhibition (HI), and virus neutralization assays as well as viral protein characterization through Western blotting and the analysis of viral replication kinetics via viral growth curves.

experiments.name: Isolation of the virus from the sample
Quantification of virus by Real-Time PCR (qPCR)
Plaque assay for the quantification of the virus
Quantification of virus by TCID₅₀ assay
Western Blot analysis for the detection of viral proteins

PG: Learners interested in concepts of Virology

objective:
To impart theoretical understanding and virtual hands-on training in isolating, propagating, quantifying, and molecularly characterizing viruses, as well as evaluating host immune responses and neutralization titers safely without biosafety hazards.
  • Master how viruses are detected and measured: Help students understand both traditional benchmark assays (like plaque counting and hemagglutination) and modern molecular tools (such as qPCR and Western blotting), learning when and why to use each technique.
  • Make the viral life cycle tangible: Move beyond textbook diagrams by letting students track viral replication step-by-step, seeing how a virus attaches, multiplies inside host cells, and releases new particles over time.
  • Learn quantitative analysis and observation firsthand: Allow students to spot real cytopathic effects under a microscope, count plaques, and work through standard calculation methods (like PFU/mL and TCID50) at their own pace and in a risk-free environment.

courseAlignment.description: The syllabi of this lab aligns to the following universities in India.
universities: The Techniques in Virology is particularly relevant to undergraduate programs in Biosciences and Bioengineering, Biotechnology, Microbiology, and allied life sciences. The laboratory directly supports and complements the learning outcomes of courses including Microbiology (BS203), Genetics (BS205) and Cell and Molecular Biology (BS209) and Immunology and Immunotechnology (PC206).
